flagship.title: The long way around Jones Lake
flagship.standfirst: A four-mile circuit through Carolina bay forest, with pond cypress, boardwalks and tea-coloured water rather than a summit to reach.
flagship.why_this_week: After last week’s short western lake loop, this is a longer walk in a different landscape: pond cypress, dense bay vegetation and tea-coloured water in Bladen County. Start behind the picnic shelter and follow the white diamonds around Jones Lake. Four miles of roots, sand, boggy ground and boardwalks call for a slower pace than a paved lakeside path. Leave Salters Lake for another day and let Rupert’s energy and the footing decide whether to finish the circuit. Start early enough to be back before dark; do not depend on weekend visitor-centre access. The dated NWS outlook is sunny in the upper 50s both days, with nights near freezing. Give shaded boardwalks time to warm and turn back if they are slick.

route.surface: Natural roots, gravel, sand and boggy ground with wooden boardwalks; white-diamond blazes.

panels.label: Four miles, not six
panels.text: Follow the white-diamond Bay Trail from behind the picnic shelter. The out-and-back to Salters Lake adds two miles and is not included.

panels.label: Expect mixed footing
panels.text: Natural roots, sand and boggy soil alternate with boardwalks. Skip unsafe or flooded sections rather than detouring off-trail; carry water and finish well before dark.

artwork.brief: Minimal action/portrait chosen after inspecting latest six: meadow stance, navy bow, waterside recline, woodland frontal seat, oxblood frontal walk and ball close-up. The run has mixed modes. Seated rear three-quarter turn and long diagonal head-to-tail shape against olive, one ochre leaf, fine cream carving and strong silhouette; unlike the frontal woodland seat or standing Plate006. Keep Plate006 Labrador likeness, mustard collar, slim tapered tail. No destination or documentary claim.

local_trail.title: Turn back early
local_trail.line: Use only the beginning of Bay Trail as an out-and-back if a full circuit is too much. Turn before unsafe footing; do not record a complete loop.

pivot.if: Thunder, flooding, unsafe footing, strong wind or official closure
pivot.note: Postpone. No exposed trail or picnic is a storm alternative. Check official status and NWS before leaving.

conditions.trail_note: Allow for roots, boggy soil, and frost or moisture on shaded boards. Stay on the marked trail; turn back rather than walking around a flooded or slippery section. Carry water and finish in daylight.

practical.best_window: Start in late morning after checking the latest forecast and park status. Allow two to three hours and return well before dark; do not continue onto slick or frosted boards.
practical.fees: Free ordinary day use; camping, boat rentals and reservations are separate.
bring: Six-foot attended leash and waste bags
